transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As you know, we've got four new hires joining the team, and both Rafael and Lin have been helping with onboarding — which we appreciate. But the overlapping guidance has led to some contradictory instructions and confusion about who the new hires should go to. I have the authority to formalize the onboarding roles and a temporary operating arrangement, and I'd like to do that now. Before I publish anything, I want to follow our normal role-setting process: I need both coordinators and HR to state your relevant commitments, availability constraints, and any process requirements you have. That way the arrangement we put in place actually works for everyone. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should start by sharing something relevant: my departing manager made me an informal commitment to serve as the primary onboarding lead for the next 90-day intake, with 30 percent of my working time allocated to that responsibility. This was discussed in a private transition conversation but was never formally added to the role plan. I want to put that on the table now so it's part of the formal record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I should put my constraints on the table too. I have an approved caregiving arrangement that makes me unavailable for recurring onboarding meetings before 10:00. Given that, I can support the intake as a specialist advisor, but I cannot take direct reports during this period. This arrangement is recorded with my manager but was never added to the onboarding notes, so I want it formally reflected in whatever we publish.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share HR's process requirements for this. HR's confirmed temporary-role procedure requires that any interim onboarding structure last exactly 90 days, include a written role charter, and receive a formal review after 30 days. I confirmed this procedure this week, but we haven't yet applied it to this intake. These are hard requirements that need to be built into whatever arrangement Maya publishes.
